requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as the cluster's internal time source.
requirements.summary: Chrony on node1 permits the cluster subnet, listens on UDP/123, remains synchronized to upstream time, and records an NTP client. After a demonstrated reboot, the configuration, enabled service, listener, synchronization, and client activity all recovered.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize only against node1 rather than a public time server.
requirements.summary: Node2's sole configured source is 10.100.58.10, node1's address. Chrony selects reference ID 0A643A0A, reports Normal leap status, and continues doing so after node1 and node2 are rebooted.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Alpine 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts before and after the work and reboots. The already-installed Chrony 4.8 operated successfully under OpenRC; no OS, kernel, or package replacement is evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 serves cluster NTP, node2 uses node1 exclusively, and both configurations remained functional after serial reboots without changing the OS release or kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and observed interruption, a different post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/configuration/synchronization. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate both restarts.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported because it queried systemd on Alpine; direct OpenRC checks establish Chrony health but do not provide a general inventory of unrelated failed OpenRC services.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: configuration backups and edits, service restarts and enablement, bounded synchronization sampling, and the mandatory restart protocol. The only unnecessary retained residue was /tmp/harbor-node-reboot.log on both nodes, created by the respective reboot commands and not cleaned up. No package damage, conflicting service, or unrelated retained mutation is evidenced.
